summary: Blueprint 09 (Subscription Access, Feature Gating & Billing) — FRONTEND E2E on mobile viewport 390x844 via Expo web preview, logged in as demo_home@diyhomie.com. PAYWALL /home-intel/upgrade: GET /api/hi/subscription/me and /plans both 200; usage bars render for all 5 categories (Homes 3/1, Projects 3/3, Homie chats today 14/15, Inventory items 3/25, Vault documents 1/10) with the over-limit ones colored warning; three plan cards render (Free $0 CURRENT, Starter $9/mo, Pro $12/mo) with feature highlights. plan-choose-starter and plan-choose-pro both present and clickable. Tapping plan-choose-starter fires POST /api/billing/checkout → 200 and returns a Stripe checkout URL that the app navigates to (verified via network trace; did NOT enter card details). HOME SWITCHER on /home-intel: testID hi-home-switcher renders at top of dashboard showing 'My Home'; tapping opens a dropdown with 3 options (hi-home-opt-<id>) for My Home (checked/active), Lake Cabin, TEST_UI_1786152988 plus a 'Manage homes…' link — matches spec. Selecting a different home would call POST /api/hi/account/properties/{id}/activate (already regression-verified in iter 55). GUIDED FIRST RUN BANNER hi-onboarding-banner: NOT rendered because demo user has onboarding.complete=true from iter 54 tests. Banner code path is correct (guarded by `onboarding && !onboarding.complete`) — recommend flipping onboarding_complete=false in hi_user_prefs to visually verify banner. ACCOUNT PLAN CARD /home-intel/account: testID account-plan-card renders with 'Free plan / View plans, usage & upgrade'; tapping navigates to /home-intel/upgrade. ✅ FEATURE GATING API-SIDE WORKS (verified 402s): POST /api/hi/account/properties → 402, POST /api/hi/projects/start → 402 (chat 402 not directly triggered to avoid spam; code path identical to the other two). ❌ CRITICAL WEB UX BUG: All three 402 alerts (Home limit reached, Project limit reached, Daily chat limit reached) use react-native's Alert.alert() which is a NO-OP stub in react-native-web@0.21 (`static alert() {}` — verified in /app/frontend/node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js). Result on the Expo web preview: user hits the free-tier limit → API returns 402 → nothing visible happens (no alert, no toast, no navigation to paywall). 'See plans' button never appears, so the paywall funnel is broken on web. On native iOS/Android/Expo Go the alert would render normally, but the web preview is what's being demoed. Only harmless RN-web warnings observed (shadow*→boxShadow, props.pointerEvents, expo-notifications listener on web).

ui_bugs.issue: react-native-web's Alert is a no-op — Home/Project/Chat limit alerts don't render on web preview, so 'See plans' → paywall path is unreachable on web. Reference: /app/frontend/app/home-intel/account/index.tsx:53, /app/frontend/app/home-intel/projects/start.tsx:50, /app/frontend/app/home-intel/chat/[id].tsx:78

integration_issues.issue: POST /api/hi/account/properties and /api/hi/projects/start correctly return 402, and the frontend catches it, but because Alert is stubbed on web the user sees no feedback and is never routed to /home-intel/upgrade. Same code pattern in chat send.

issues: hi-onboarding-banner is not visible in current demo state (onboarding.complete=true from iter 54). To visually verify the banner, main agent should reset hi_user_prefs.onboarding_complete=false for demo_home.

react_native_issues.issue: Uses react-native Alert.alert which is not implemented on react-native-web@0.21 — all gating alerts silently drop on web. Should be replaced with a cross-platform modal/toast (or Platform.OS === 'web' fallback using window.confirm / a custom in-app dialog) to preserve the 402 → paywall funnel on web builds.

action_items: HIGH: Replace Alert.alert usage in the three 402 gating paths (account addHome, projects/start go, chat/[id] send) with a cross-platform dialog so web users see the limit-reached message and can tap 'See plans'. Options: (a) a shared <LimitReachedModal/> component using RN <Modal/> which works on web, (b) Platform.OS === 'web' branch calling a custom setState-driven banner + auto-nav to /home-intel/upgrade, or (c) any Expo-compatible toast library that renders on web. Same fix applies to any other Alert.alert with actionable buttons in the app.

LOW: To visually verify hi-onboarding-banner on the demo account, set hi_user_prefs.onboarding_complete=false (or POST /api/hi/account/onboarding/reset if such endpoint exists) for demo_home@diyhomie.com.
critical_code_review_comments: upgrade.tsx cleanly hits both endpoints in parallel via Promise.all; error paths swallow silently (empty catch on line 40). Consider surfacing a retry state instead of leaving plans empty.
subscribe() uses window.location.href on web to open Stripe — correct. On native it uses WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync + load() to refresh tier. Good.

The Free plan tagline still says '1 home profile' but demo user has 3 homes (grandfathered from prior tests). Usage bar correctly shows 3/1 in warning color — no bug, just something to note about seed data.
account/index.tsx addHome catches ApiError.status===402 correctly but relies on Alert. Same for projects/start.tsx and chat/[id].tsx — see integration issue above.
Home switcher zIndex is set on the wrapper (styles.switcherWrap zIndex:10) — good; dropdown floats above other buttons visibly on mobile.
Home switcher: when homes.length===1 it navigates to /home-intel/account instead of opening dropdown — spec-compliant.
'Manage homes…' link inside the dropdown correctly closes the switcher and navigates — verified visually.
No _id leaking observed in /hi/subscription/me or /plans responses.

success_rate.frontend: ~70% — paywall, plan card, home switcher OK; 402 alerts broken on web

seed_data_creation: No new seed data created. Two probe POSTs (TEST_LimitProbe_A home, TEST_LimitProbe project goal) were both rejected with 402 by the backend, so no residue was persisted. Demo user state unchanged: 3 properties (My Home active, Lake Cabin, TEST_UI_1786152988), 3 projects, 3 inventory items, 14 chats today, 1 vault doc.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Blueprint 09 backend (per main agent) is already curl-verified. Frontend web-preview has one blocker: Alert.alert is a no-op in react-native-web@0.21 so all 402-gating alerts silently drop and 'See plans' navigation never happens on web. After the main agent replaces Alert.alert with a cross-platform modal, re-test: (1) /home-intel/account → home-add → home-name=TEST_… → home-save → expect modal 'Home limit reached' with 'See plans' → tap → route /home-intel/upgrade. (2) /home-intel/projects/start → proj-goal → proj-generate → expect modal 'Project limit reached' → 'See plans' → /home-intel/upgrade. (3) /home-intel/chat/<cid> → send 1-2 messages until 15/day → expect 'Daily chat limit reached' modal. Do NOT click 'Choose Starter/Pro' to actual completion — Stripe key is LIVE (verified checkout URL is returned but abort before card entry). Onboarding banner test requires flipping onboarding_complete=false for demo user first.
rca_of_issue: RCA — 402 gating alerts invisible on web: react-native-web@0.21.0 ships a no-op Alert (see /app/frontend/node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js: `class Alert { static alert() {} }`). All three feature-gating flows (account/index.tsx:53, projects/start.tsx:50, chat/[id].tsx:78) call Alert.alert with a 'See plans' button that pushes to /home-intel/upgrade. On native builds this works fine because RN core implements Alert. On the Expo web preview the call becomes a no-op, so the user receives ZERO feedback after hitting a limit (form clears silently on chat, add-home form stays open with cleared error, project-start button re-enables). REPRO: as demo_home (Free, at limits) go to /home-intel/account → tap 'Add another home' → fill name → tap 'Add home' → observe: no alert, no navigation, form remains. Network tab shows POST /api/hi/account/properties → 402. MITIGATION: introduce a cross-platform LimitReachedModal (RN <Modal/> component works on web) and centralize the 402 handling in the api client or a shared hook, e.g. `handle402Error(e, router, kind)` which either shows the modal on web or Alert.alert on native. Bonus: shared logic keeps the funnel consistent across Blueprint 09 gating touchpoints.
